query: Reported superconducting high-entropy alloys are dominated by Nb-Ta matrices, while other studies concern titanium-rich systems based on heavy transition metals and partly ordered systems. Consequently, these precedents do not establish what controls superconductivity in high-entropy alloys outside the best-studied material classes. Within the defining constraint of a solid solution containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each, what governs superconducting behavior in such an uncharacterized high-entropy alloy, and why? State one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison against the starting material, predicted observations relative to the baseline, applicable boundary conditions, the earlier evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In a homogeneous high‐entropy alloy with a random bcc structure, superconducting behavior is governed by the interplay of the averaged electron‐phonon coupling—which depends on the weighted density-of-states at the Fermi level—and mass disorder–induced phonon softening. This balance sets the critical temperature and upper critical field.
generation.material_initial_state: A single-phase, bcc high-entropy alloy solid solution (e.g., composition similar to Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08) where all five or more elements are randomly distributed at ≥5 at.% each.
generation.intervention: Systematically vary the relative atomic percentages of heavy transition metals and titanium (while keeping a minimum of 5 at.% for each) to modulate both the average electron count and the mass disorder.
generation.conditions: Experiments conducted at cryogenic temperatures (around the superconducting transition temperature) and under applied magnetic fields, with constant synthesis conditions to preserve a single-phase bcc structure.
generation.structural_mediator: The random atomic site occupancy in a bcc lattice, which produces local variations in atomic mass and bonding, mediating both the effective density-of-states and phonon spectrum.
generation.mechanism: The hypothesis posits that the electron-phonon interaction, crucial for conventional BCS superconductivity in these HEAs, is controlled by a weighted contribution of each element’s electronic states and the disorder-induced modulation of phonon modes. The balance between an optimal density-of-states and sufficient phonon softening enhances electron-phonon coupling, thus determining superconducting properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Alloys adjusted to increase the average atomic mass and optimize the electronic density-of-states will exhibit enhanced electron-phonon coupling, leading to a higher Tc and/or increased upper critical fields relative to a baseline composition. Conversely, deviations that disrupt this balance (either too low or too high electron count or disorder) will lower superconducting performance.
generation.baseline: The original high-entropy alloy (e.g., Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08) or other Nb-Ta based HEA systems with reported Tc around 7.5 K and μ0Hc2 near 12 T, representing the standard superconducting performance in well-studied compositions.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies as long as the alloy remains a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution in the bcc structure and is in the dirty limit (i.e., high scattering from disorder). It may not hold if compositional changes induce phase separation or significant short-range order that alters the electron-phonon interaction qualitatively.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative relationship linking individual elemental contributions to the density-of-states and the detailed effects of mass disorder on phonon dispersion remains uncertain. Moreover, potential short-range ordering upon compositional adjustment might also influence the superconducting properties in ways not fully captured by this hypothesis.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of HEAs by varying the relative atomic percentages of heavy transition metals and titanium while keeping all constituents above 5 at.%. Use X-ray diffraction to confirm the maintenance of a single-phase bcc structure. Measure the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) and upper critical magnetic field (Hc2) as a function of composition. Additionally, characterize the density-of-states (using tunneling spectroscopy) and phonon spectra (using inelastic neutron scattering) to correlate them with superconducting performance.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the variations in electron count and mass disorder do not produce predictable changes in Tc and Hc2 according to the changes in the measured density-of-states or phonon softening—or if local ordering rather than averaged disorder is found to dominate superconducting properties—the hypothesis will be falsified.

## Abstract
The structural and physical properties of the new titanium- and niobium-rich type-A high-entropy alloy (HEA) superconductor Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08 (in at.%) were studied by X-ray powder diffraction, energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, magnetization, electrical resistivity, and specific heat measurements. In addition, electronic structure calculations were performed using two complementary methods: the Korringa–Kohn–Rostoker Coherent Potential Approximation (KKR-CPA) and the Projector Augmented Wave (PAW) within Density Functional Theory (DFT). The results obtained indicate that the alloy exhibits type II superconductivity with a critical temperature close to 7.5 K, an intermediate electron–phonon coupling, and an upper critical field of 12.2(1) T. This finding indicates that Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08 has one of the highest upper critical fields among all known HEA superconductors.

## Abstract
AbstractHigh-entropy alloys (HEA) form through the random arrangement of five or more chemical elements on a crystalline lattice. Despite the significant amount of resulting compositional disorder, a subset of HEAs enters a superconducting state below critical temperatures, Tc<10 K. The superconducting properties of the known HEAs seem to suffice a Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer (BCS) description, but little is known about their superconducting order parameter and the microscopic role of disorder. We report on magnetic susceptibility measurements on films of the superconducting HEA (TaNb)1-x(ZrHfTi)x for characterizing the lower and upper critical fields Hc,1(T) and Hc,2(T), respectively as a function of temperature T. Our resulting analysis of the Ginzburg–Landau coherence length and penetration depth demonstrates that HEAs of this type are single-band isotropic s-wave superconductors in the dirty limit. Despite a significant difference in the elemental composition between the x=0.35 and x=0.71 films, we find that the observed Tc variations cannot be explained by disorder effects.Subject terms: Condensed-matter physics, Superconducting properties and materials
